_: The style of “The Power of the Incomprehensible” (docs/stories/sila-nepost.md): reality — 1910s expressionist silent cinema (painted flats with broken perspective and painted shadows, actors in make-up), b/w toned per scene, flicker, scratches, dust, 18 fps; when that music plays, the image comes through in autochrome colour. So the pictures are drawn IN COLOUR (the pastel palette of an autochrome plate), and the b/w and toning are done by the stage: stage.saturation 0 + tint, the transition — grade_to in the light preset. Photographic edges (key: soft), no shadows from the flats — the shadows are painted on the sets.
cutout: Photographed like an actor in a European silent film of the 1910s: pale powdered silent-film make-up with darkened eyes and lips, expressive theatrical mime, captured on an early autochrome colour plate (Lumière autochrome): soft pastel, slightly faded colours (dusty rose, sage green, ochre, violet-grey, Prussian blue), delicate starch-grain texture, gentle softness, soft studio daylight. Natural photographic edges: no outline, no white border, no paper margin, not a drawing, not a cut-out, not a sticker. The whole subject fully visible, nothing cropped.
cutout_bg: Isolated on a perfectly flat, uniform pure chroma-green (#00FF00) background — nothing else in the image: no room, no wall, no window, no floor, no ground, no shadow.
